subject.title: [Bug]: ${VAR} shell parameter expansion mangles env var values containing ## in Discord channel runtime context

question: Should OpenClaw investigate this as a Discord-bound exec env security bug by capturing redacted live proof before any fix lane, or close it later as unsupported if no Discord-bound reproduction can be produced?
rationale: The report involves password-like environment data changing in an agent shell path, but current source and direct shell checks do not prove a mutation point, so automation should not choose or implement a secret/env behavior change speculatively.

options.title: Capture redacted Discord proof
options.body: Run or request a redacted Discord-bound Docker exec transcript that compares `${SOME_PASSWORD}` with `$(printenv SOME_PASSWORD)` before selecting a fix boundary.

options.title: Ask reporter for fresh evidence
options.body: Leave the issue open but require the reporter to provide a short redacted screenshot, recording, or logs from current OpenClaw before maintainers spend live-test time.

options.title: Close later if still unproven
options.body: If no Discord-bound reproduction or source root cause emerges after a defined follow-up window, close as unsupported with the direct shell/source evidence.

recommendation.title: Capture redacted Discord proof
recommendation.body: Run or request a redacted Discord-bound Docker exec transcript that compares `${SOME_PASSWORD}` with `$(printenv SOME_PASSWORD)` before selecting a fix boundary.
